sections.title: What every ClickMasters AI API includes

blocks.heading: Security and access control
paragraphs: OAuth 2.0 or API-key authentication, role-based permissions, tenant isolation, secrets management, input sanitization and prompt-injection defenses for LLM endpoints.

blocks.heading: Rate limiting and cost control
paragraphs: Per-client rate limits and quotas protect both your infrastructure and your upstream model budget. Caching, model routing and token budgets keep inference spend predictable.

blocks.heading: Versioning, documentation and observability
paragraphs: Versioned endpoints with OpenAPI specifications, request tracing, latency and error dashboards, model-quality monitoring and alerting — so changes to models or prompts never silently break consumers.

items.question: What is an AI API?
items.answer: An AI API is an application programming interface that exposes an AI capability — a prediction, classification, generated text, image analysis or retrieval result — so other software can call it over the network. It packages the model with the authentication, validation, scaling and monitoring needed for production use.

items.question: How much does AI API development cost?
items.answer: A single-model inference API typically costs $15,000–$35,000. LLM orchestration and RAG APIs usually run $20,000–$80,000, and a developer-facing platform with SDKs and documentation $60,000–$180,000.

items.question: Why not call OpenAI or Anthropic directly from our app?
items.answer: An internal AI API layer centralizes keys and access control, enforces rate limits and budgets, validates outputs, logs usage for audit, and lets you switch or combine model providers without changing every client application.

items.question: Can you deploy the API in our cloud?
items.answer: Yes. We deploy on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud in your account — or on-premise — using containers and infrastructure-as-code so your team can operate it.

items.question: Do you provide documentation and SDKs?
items.answer: Every API ships with an OpenAPI specification and usage documentation. Client SDKs and a developer portal are included in platform engagements and available as add-ons for smaller projects.

items.question: Who owns the API code?
items.answer: You do — complete IP transfer of source code, infrastructure configuration and documentation at project completion.
